title: Geologic map of the Privateer quadrangle, Clarendon and Sumter Counties, South Carolina
citation: W.R. Doar, III, 2015, Geologic map of the Privateer quadrangle, Clarendon and Sumter Counties, South Carolina: South Carolina Geological Survey Open-File Report 217, map scale 1:24,000.
notes:
Single OCR map sheet; map face is noise. Symbol-to-unit links inferred from OCR layout (flagged). Symbols for moved earth ('[me'), Duplin lower part ('[neat') and Lang Syne ('[Fete') are illegible. Freshwater marsh thickness '| to 40 feet' not recorded (first digit unreadable). Bodies of water skipped.
SUBSURFACE: page 1 has cross section A-A' (vertical exaggeration 50, scale 120-220 feet / 18-30 meters) with SCGS drill holes Pi-1, Pi-14, Pi-16, Pi-26, Pi-31 and Pi-35 along it (drill holes within one mile of the line are projected; dashed where farther); units shown along it include Qe, Qcb, QHfw, NPdu and PEs; logs are on file at SCGS and not printed. Map symbols also show drill holes Pi-31 and Pi-34. Duplin Formation inland limit at +220 ft (+67.5 m) in the map area (page 1). Vertical datum not stated; base map uses 1927 North American Datum, contour interval 2 meters.
Re-read of page 1 for subsurface fields (single OCR map sheet; map face is noise). Units as before; map symbols read from the legend boxes on page-image tiles (legend prints 'Ppls', section labels 'PPls'); freshwater marsh thickness OCR '| to 40 feet' read as 1 (inferred). Duplin inland limit +220 ft recorded as a stated top (no vertical datum printed). Cross section A-A' read from page-image tiles (crop of the section strip, 144 dpi): 13 drill holes; unit intervals are elevations read off the section's own feet scale (inferred, about +/-1 ft), units identified by the labelled colours. Solid holes (within one mile of the line) Pi-1, Pi-3, Pi-16, Pi-25, Pi-34 get a land-surface elevation (cap within about 2 ft of the profile); dashed holes (more than one mile away) get no land-surface elevation and no top for their first interval. The section prints no horizontal scale, so no distances or contact lines are recorded; no vertical datum printed. Map-face drill holes (Pi-xx) carry labels only (logs on file at SCGS). Bodies of water and legend-only symbols not recorded.
